newsitem.title: USA: Quaker says Snapple sales fell in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Quaker says Snapple sales fell in 1996.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said Thursday its Snapple beverage business saw an eight percent decline in U.S. and Canadian sales in 1996, with volumes down 11 percent.
Snapple continued to operate at a cash loss, reflecting volume declines and increased promotional spending, Quaker said.
Diet Snapple sales increased 23 percent in 1996, it said.
"The six-flavor Diet Snapple line has grown from seven to 12 percent of Snapple's sales, and we believe that could grow to 25 percent in the future," Quaker Chairman William Smithburg said.

Quaker said its overall beverage business in 1996 -- U.S., Canadian and international operations -- posted opreating income of $54.7 million. This compares with a loss of $39.1 million in 1995, which included restructuring charges.
A five percent sales gain for Gatorade sports drink in the U.S. and Canada last year was offset by lower European and Snapple volumes, it said.
Total beverage sales declined two percent in 1996 to $1.93 billion as volumes declined four percent.
U.S. and Canadian beverage operating income was $84.4 million, up from $18.9 million in 1995. Excluding charges, operating income nearly doubled, to $101.0 million from $51.3 million.
U.S. and Canadian beverage sales in 1996 of $1.61 billion were up one percent from 1995.
U.S. and Canadian operating income rose due to a four percent volume increase and "excellent" margin improvement for Gatorade, Quaker said.
"Gatorade's performance was outstanding, especially in a year that was expected to be even more challenging due to competition," Smithburg said.

International beverages posted an operating loss of $29.7 million in 1996, reflecting costs to continue Gatorade expansion, especially in the Asia/Pacific region, and a strategic pull-back of Snapple in international markets.

This compared with an operating loss of $58.0 million in 1995, which included $14.5 million in restructuring charges. International beverage sales fell 11 percent to $314.0 million in 1996, reflecting a restructuring of European Gatorade to focus on southern Europe, the pull-back of Snapple, and lower sales to licensee markets in the Asia/Pacific region.
"The Gatorade launch in China is going well and we foresee tremendous growth potential in that market," Smithburg said. "The number of international Gatorade markets has expanded to 44 countries."
